description: On-device passive authentication: the SOD CMS signature, DSC->CSCA path building, the verdict taxonomy and signed CSCA master-list ingestion. Fixtures come from the deterministic test PKI in test/support/, openssl-cross-checked (test/pki/README-fixtures.md).

cases.name: sodSignature plain rsaEncryption + SHA-256 valid
cases.description: the RFC 3370 §3.2 SignerInfo form; upstream's substring dispatch lands it on its SHA-256 default, so only this digest verifies there

cases.name: sodSignature SHA-1 v1.5 valid
cases.description: both runners accept SHA-1; the weak_digest annotation is dart-only surface and does not change the outcome

cases.name: sodSignature ECDSA with non-minimal INTEGERs
cases.description: upstream repairs the leading-zero r/s in place (OpenSSLUtils.swift:456-520); the port accepts them on decode. NOTE: a bare `openssl cms -verify` rejects this fixture; neither runner uses that path

cases.name: sodSignature signedAttrs absent
cases.description: upstream's manual walk cannot find the signed attributes and throws; the port reports malformed_sod

cases.name: trust RSA DSC under its CSCA
trust EC DSC under its CSCA
trust explicit-params EC DSC
cases.description: OpenSSL 3 raises X509_V_ERR_EC_KEY_EXPLICIT_PARAMS and upstream's verify callback ignores exactly that error; the port reaches the same answer through the explicit-params SPKI arm

cases.name: trust CSCA link certificate chain
cases.description: DSC -> CSCA(new, link) -> CSCA(old, self-signed anchor)

cases.name: trust case-differing issuer DN
cases.description: the DSC carries no AKI and its issuer DN differs from the anchor's subject only in case/whitespace; OpenSSL's X509_NAME_cmp canonicalizes, and the port's DN compare does too

cases.name: trust DSC as its own anchor
cases.description: upstream requires nrCertsInChain > 1, so a self-signed DSC sitting in the store fails even though it is trusted

cases.name: verify valid document, all three booleans true
verify corrupted signature keeps the other two true
cases.description: upstream swallows the signature failure entirely and compares hashes over the unverified content anyway; only this boolean records it

cases.name: RSASSA-PSS SHA-384 document verifies (dart)
cases.description: the port reads the RFC 4055 parameters; the fixture is openssl-cms-verified

cases.name: RSASSA-PSS SHA-384 document fails (swift)
cases.description: upstream hard-codes SHA-256 for every rsassaPss signature (OpenSSLUtils.swift:448 + 534-537), so a legitimately signed SHA-384 PSS document false-negatives

cases.name: plain rsaEncryption + SHA-512 verifies (dart)
cases.description: the digest comes from the SignerInfo digestAlgorithm (RFC 3370 §3.2)

cases.name: plain rsaEncryption + SHA-512 fails (swift)
cases.description: the algorithm long name "rsaEncryption" matches none of the substring arms, so upstream verifies with its SHA-256 default

cases.name: DSA signature algorithm is unsupported, not a bad signature
cases.description: both runners answer false; only the port distinguishes "unsupported" from "invalid"; see the pa.verdict twin

cases.name: eContentType is not id-ldsSecurityObject (swift accepts)
cases.description: upstream navigates the CMS purely positionally and checks no OIDs anywhere, so the signature still verifies

cases.name: content-type attribute mismatch (dart rejects)
cases.description: RFC 5652 §5.3 MUST; upstream never reads the attribute

cases.name: verdict corrupted signature is reported, not swallowed
verdict DSC as its own anchor
certless SOD is malformed_sod, not a crash
cases.description: upstream force-unwraps certs[0] (NFCPassportModel.swift:412, SOD.swift:96) and crashes the app

cases.name: hostile CMS body is a verdict, not a throw
sodSignature detail SHA-1 is annotated weak_digest
trust detail valid chain reports the terminal anchor
trust detail link chain reports the old anchor
masterList BER indefinite lengths
cases.description: real .ml files carry indefinite lengths; TlvRecord rejects them by design, which is why the pki layer has its own ASN.1 substrate

cases.name: masterList pinned by the signer's issuer
masterList wrong signer accepted with allowUnpinned
masterList unpinned without the escape hatch is refused
masterList eContentType .1 instead of .2 is refused
masterList with a broken signature is refused before pinning
masterList unparseable entry is skipped and counted
masterList garbage input is a typed parse error
